question: an above the line deduction refers to a deduction for agi
answer: [791074244_984-1834] An above-the-line deduction refers to a deduction for gross income in the context of the Internal Revenue Service's rules, which are subtracted before calculating adjusted gross income. This deduction is not dependent on adjusted gross income and can be claimed by all taxpayers regardless of their itemized deductions.

Certain below the line deductions are also phased out for high income taxpayers pursuant to Internal Revenue Code Section 68 . Medical and dental expenses are below the line deductions pursuant to Internal Revenue Code Section 67 . These expenses may only be deducted , however , to the extent they exceed 10 % ( 7.5 % for 65 and over ) of a taxpayer 's AGI . Above - the - line deductions are also preferred because they can be taken by ALL taxpayers regardless of whether they take standard or itemized deductions ( see attached tax ladder ) . Moreover , they are desirable because they reduce adjusted gross income ( AGI ) . Generally , the smaller the AGI , the greater the percentage of deductibility of itemized deductions .
